newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Abbey chief warns about mortgage relief cut.
newsitem.headline: Abbey chief warns about mortgage relief cut.

text.p: Any possible abolition of British tax relief on mortgage interest needs careful study as it could hurt many Britons, said the chief executive of one of Britain's largest mortgage lenders.
Peter Birch, chief executive of Abbey National plc, warned that the new Labour government should bear this in mind when it brings forward its budget measures, widely expected by early July.
Birch said that City practitioners need to look outside affluent London and the south of England for the real impact of such a move.
"You need to look more broadly. A lot of people live in areas where mortgage tax relief is a very important factor," he said.
He said that 60-70 percent of the population have the basic 30,000 stg mortgage which attracts tax relief, saving individuals 300-400 stg a year which Birch described as a "significant sum".
But he said phasing in the abolition of relief would help people cope better and recognise the desire to eliminate subsidies.

He said he expects a further 0.25 point rise in UK base rates from the current 6.25 percent level. He said the housing market in the south of England remains buoyant with a shortage of property for sale and that elsewhere it is firmer.

Birch said lending margins were stabilising after falling in the first quarter. Turnover in the housing market is expected to rise this year to between 20 and 22 billion stg from 18 billion in 1996, he said. He was speaking at a banking seminar sponsored by NCR.
